summary.headline: Best UK opportunity today: compliance-led workflow automation sold as a productized service, with niche SME AI ops automation the strongest non-compliance play.
summary.best_opportunity: Making Tax Digital catch-up and 2027 onboarding workflows
summary.why_now: Live GOV.UK guidance still gives a direct buying trigger: qualifying income above £50,000 moved into Making Tax Digital from 6 April 2026, above £30,000 starts from 6 April 2027, and above £20,000 starts from 6 April 2028. That creates a practical service wedge now for setup, reminders and ongoing admin support.

top_opportunities.name: Making Tax Digital catch-up and 2027 onboarding workflows
top_opportunities.description: Sell fixed-scope setup, bookkeeping-tool integration, reminder automation, exception handling and quarterly admin support for accountants, bookkeepers, sole traders and landlords affected by Making Tax Digital for Income Tax.
top_opportunities.why_now: Live GOV.UK guidance says qualifying income over £50,000 for tax year 2024 to 2025 had to move onto MTD from 6 April 2026, over £30,000 for 2025 to 2026 starts from 6 April 2027, and over £20,000 for 2026 to 2027 starts from 6 April 2028. That is a real compliance deadline rather than speculative demand.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small accountancy firms, bookkeepers, self-employed professionals and landlords
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High - onboarding fee plus monthly or quarterly support retainers
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong for a solo engineer if positioned as workflow tooling and admin automation rather than tax advice.
risks: Accounting software vendors already own the core ledger, so the wedge is onboarding and workflow support rather than bookkeeping itself
The offer must avoid regulated tax-advice positioning unless paired with an accountant
top_opportunities.verdict: Best immediate-cash opportunity because the demand is deadline-led, easy to explain, and can be sold before building any substantial software product.

top_opportunities.name: Companies House identity-verification workflow service
top_opportunities.description: Offer identity-verification onboarding, document collection, reminder workflows, status tracking and lightweight client portals for accountants, incorporation agents and company-secretarial firms.
top_opportunities.why_now: Live GOV.UK pages say the voluntary window opened in 2025, more than 6 million individuals would need to comply in the 12 months after the requirement took effect, and current guidance says directors and PSCs provide a Companies House personal code through the confirmation-statement flow. That creates admin-heavy recurring work for firms serving many entities.
top_opportunities.buyer: Accountants, company-secretarial firms, formation agents and compliance providers
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium to high - onboarding projects plus reminders and annual compliance admin retainers
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good for a solo engineer comfortable building internal ops tools and simple customer-facing dashboards.
risks: Process details can change, so templates and messaging need periodic updates
The niche is narrower than generic SME automation, so outreach must be highly targeted
top_opportunities.verdict: One of the clearest niche B2B opportunities because the legal workflow is live, repetitive and painful for firms handling many directors or PSCs.

top_opportunities.name: AI back-office automation for UK professional-service SMEs
top_opportunities.description: Package one repeatable workflow outcome for firms like recruiters, mortgage brokers, accountants or surveyors: inbox-to-CRM, call-summary-to-task creation, document intake, compliance reminders or draft report generation.
top_opportunities.why_now: The non-compliance evidence is broader but still live. GOV.UK's SME Digital Adoption Taskforce final report says digital tools can improve productivity by 7 to 18 per cent per technology, and its 2026 update keeps pushing adoption to improve SME productivity. That supports practical AI-assisted admin automation sold as a narrow productized service.
top_opportunities.buyer: Admin-heavy professional-service SMEs with repetitive client intake and follow-up work
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High - implementation fee plus monitoring, support and change-request retainer
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Excellent for a solo engineer because it can start service-first on existing APIs, then turn into reusable templates or micro-SaaS.
risks: Generic AI automation is crowded, so the offer must stay narrow by vertical and workflow
Evidence is strong on productivity demand but weaker on which exact niche buys first, so founder-led validation still matters
top_opportunities.verdict: Best tech-enabled long-term play if sold as one workflow for one niche instead of a general AI agency offer.

top_opportunities.name: Quoting, scheduling and follow-up automation for field-service SMEs
top_opportunities.description: Sell a productized stack for trades and field-service firms that improves lead capture, quote turnaround, scheduling, reminders and review requests without replacing their full job-management platform.
top_opportunities.why_now: Live market-page evidence from CompareSoft says 8,961 field teams have used it to shortlist field-service software and frames the category around replacing spreadsheets, whiteboards and paper job sheets. That suggests many buyers still need implementation and process automation rather than another full SaaS platform.
top_opportunities.buyer: Plumbers, electricians, HVAC firms, cleaning firms, pest control and similar field-service SMEs
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: High - setup plus monthly support, reporting and messaging retainers
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good for a solo engineer because it can be delivered as repeatable workflows on top of existing tools.
risks: Some buyers already have software, so the pitch should be faster quote-to-cash rather than full replacement
This is best when narrowed to one trade with a repeatable template set
top_opportunities.verdict: A credible recurring-revenue business if positioned as automation and implementation for one trade, not as another generic field-service app.

top_opportunities.name: SME digital-adoption implementation sprints
top_opportunities.description: Offer fixed-price selection, setup and integration sprints for SMEs still using fragmented admin processes, especially around CRM, e-invoicing, workflow automation and reporting.
top_opportunities.why_now: Live GOV.UK research on understanding technology adoption among UK SMEs says firms still face information gaps around productivity-enhancing digital technologies, while the taskforce continues to frame digital adoption as a route to productivity growth. That supports a practical done-for-you service for small firms that know they need better systems but will not run a long software-buying process alone.
top_opportunities.buyer: Owner-managed SMEs with spreadsheet-heavy sales, admin or finance operations
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium to high - initial sprint plus ongoing admin, reporting and integration support
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong for a solo engineer who can translate messy business workflows into a simple tool stack and rollout plan.
risks: This is less urgent than compliance-led offers, so sales depend more on sharp positioning and proof
Without a niche, it can drift into low-margin general consulting
top_opportunities.verdict: Not the flashiest option, but a realistic part-time-friendly business if tightly packaged around one operational outcome and one buyer type.

best_pick.name: Making Tax Digital catch-up and 2027 onboarding workflows
best_pick.why_it_wins: It best matches the brief today: low startup cost, direct compliance demand, fast path to first invoice and strong recurring support revenue. It is less glamorous than AI SaaS, but it is easier to sell because the buyer pain is live and deadline-driven. A solo engineer can productize setup, reminders, status tracking and client communications into a repeatable service, then turn repeated pieces into a lightweight tool later.
validation_plan: Target one buyer group first, ideally small accountancy firms or bookkeepers already serving self-employed clients around the MTD thresholds.
Build a simple checklist-and-reminder demo covering client segmentation, software setup, quarterly reminders and exception handling.
Offer a fixed-price MTD catch-up or readiness sprint to 10 local firms, with an optional monthly support retainer.
After the first 3 paid clients, convert recurring steps into templates, intake forms and a lightweight dashboard.
best_pick.first_offer: MTD readiness sprint: client segmentation, bookkeeping-tool setup, reminder workflow, quarterly process template and support handover for a fixed fee plus optional monthly support.
best_pick.mvp: A thin admin panel, client-status tracker, reminder engine, templated emails and one or two bookkeeping-software integrations.
best_pick.do_today: Build one demo workflow and start targeted outreach to 30 UK accountancy or bookkeeping firms that market MTD support but do not present an automation-led service.
